scope.sharedAchievementOptimization: Only economyAction get_achievements and sync_achievement_showcase opt in. Code redemption and other ensureAchievementState callers retain eager behavior.

behavior.entry: Initial entry and post-age-confirmation entry use one state RPC, not two. Only overlapping same-lifecycle/same-UID state requests share work; settled requests do not become a persistent cache.
behavior.freshness: Successful mutations invalidate older in-flight state. Later hub navigation and explicit refresh retrieve fresh state. Late responses are fenced by lifecycle, state identity, UID and thread generation.
behavior.readReceipts: Acknowledge only events loaded by the current visible thread. Coalesce same-contract acknowledgements, use server-confirmed readSeq, retain newer unread events and preserve unread on error. No polling retry loop.
behavior.serverFastPath: Same transaction checks contract participant, age confirmation and block policy. Advancing readSeq updates only the receipt; repeated, lower or invalid seq causes no write. No change to eventSeq, updatedAt or lastEventAt.
behavior.fallback: Expired, blocked or due pending-cap contracts fall back to the full existing runner in the same transaction, preserving lazy end/refund/ledger/cap-event behavior.
behavior.achievements: Use transaction-local initialized tribute stats for unlocks, without a separate ready-state preflight read. Existing history backfill remains and retries the read transaction at most once.

measuredOrCodeDerivedReductions.metric: stats plus achievement profile document reads
measuredOrCodeDerivedReductions.evidence: Service tests and emulator transaction trace

measuredOrCodeDerivedReductions.path: Initialized common achievement check via economyAction
Ordinary read receipt with canonical block policy
measuredOrCodeDerivedReductions.evidence: Original full-runner path inspection and real Firestore emulator transaction trace of new path

caveats: These are per-path reductions, not a whole-bill savings percentage; actual production billing has not yet been measured.
Legacy block-policy fallback can still add reads. Lifecycle fallback needs full accounting reads and may read fast-path documents again.
First-time uninitialized achievement history can require an extra read transaction; savings apply to initialized steady-state users.
No-op read receipts already avoided server writes before this change; new client coalescing primarily avoids redundant requests/reads.
No RTDB listener or download optimization is included in this release.

emulator.limitations: Canonical block policy is provided by a one-document transaction-reading test dependency; no production user data accessed.

verification.independentReview: Clear after narrowing shared achievement optimization to economyAction get_achievements/sync_achievement_showcase only. No extra callable deployments.
limitations: No real production-user contracts, wallet balances or rewards were mutated for testing.
Public verification proves source delivery, startup and auth boundary; no real-account end-to-end session, smartphone test or long-play cost measurement was performed.
